lines.rookie: Two messengers said the true day: the first of April. Gwan-sun's sign was a fire on Maebong hill the night before. Gyeongsun wrote the flame note. She kept the plan in her box, and you locked it with the true days. On 1 April 1919, Gwan-sun helped lead thousands of people at Aunae Market. They called for Korea's independence.
lines.junior: Two messengers gave the real day: the first of April. Gwan-sun's sign was a fire on Maebong hill the night before. Gyeongsun, who wrote the flame note, kept the plan in her box, and you locked it with the true days. lines.master: Two messengers agreed on the real day: the first of April. Gwan-sun's sign was a fire on Maebong hill the night before. Gyeongsun, who wrote the flame note, kept the plan in her box, which you locked with the true days. On 1 April 1919, alongside the village elders, Gwan-sun helped lead thousands of people at Aunae Market, and together they called for Korea's independence.

lines.rookie: Gwan-sun's plan, written in a hurry:
lines.junior: Gwan-sun's plan, scribbled quickly:
lines.master: Gwan-sun's plan, hastily written:

lines.rookie:
When the market is full, we start the march.
In the morning, people walk to the market, like shoppers.
They come because they saw our sign the night before.
Our sign is a fire on Maebong hill.
No bell. A bell is too loud.
lines.junior:
When the market is full, we start the march.
In the morning, people walk to the market as if they are shoppers.
They come because they saw our sign the night before.
Our sign will be a fire on Maebong hill.
No bell. A bell makes too much noise.
lines.master:
When the market is full, we start the march.
In the morning, people stroll to the market, as though they were ordinary shoppers.
They come because they spotted our sign the night before.
Our sign shall be a fire on Maebong hill.
No bell: a bell would be far too loud.

lines.rookie: Gyeongsun warned you about Mr. Pyo. Now she will keep the plan.
lines.junior: Gyeongsun warned you about Mr. Pyo, and now she will keep the plan.
lines.master: Gyeongsun warned you about Mr. Pyo; now the plan is in her keeping.

lines.rookie: the night before
lines.junior: the night before
lines.master: the night before

lines.rookie: March has thirty-one days.
lines.junior: March has thirty-one days.
lines.master: March has thirty-one days.

lines.rookie: MAEBONG HILL
lines.junior: MAEBONG HILL
lines.master: MAEBONG HILL

lines.rookie: At dusk, Gyeongsun leads you up Maebong hill.
lines.junior: As the sun sets, Gyeongsun takes you up Maebong hill.
lines.master: At dusk, Gyeongsun guides you up the slope of Maebong hill.

lines.rookie: She opens her old wooden box and lays Gwan-sun's plan inside.
lines.junior: She opens her old wooden box and places Gwan-sun's plan inside it.
lines.master: She lifts the lid of her old wooden box and lays Gwan-sun's plan within.

lines.rookie: "Set the lock to our two days. The stranger only knows Mr. Pyo's day."
lines.junior: "Set the lock to our two days, so the stranger, who only knows Mr. Pyo's day, cannot open it."
lines.master: "Set the lock to our two days; the stranger knows only Mr. Pyo's day, so the box will stay shut to him."

lines.rookie: The dial lock, and Gyeongsun's words:
lines.junior: On the dial lock, and in Gyeongsun's words:
lines.master: The dial lock, and what Gyeongsun whispers:

lines.rookie:
Two map dials: the night of the sign. It is a night in March.
One clock dial: the day of the march, in April.
Remember: March has thirty-one days.
lines.junior:
The two map dials: the night of the sign, which is a night in March.
The clock dial: the day of the march, which is in April.
Don't forget: March has thirty-one days.
lines.master:
The two map dials hold the night of the sign, which falls in March.
The clock dial holds the day of the march, in April.
Bear in mind: March has thirty-one days.

lines.rookie: Set the dials: first the night of the sign, then the day of the march.
lines.junior: Set the dials: the night of the sign first, and then the day of the march.
lines.master: Set the dials: first the night the sign is lit, then the day of the march.

lines.rookie: The map dials are for the plan. The clock dial is for the day.
lines.junior: The map dials go with the plan. The clock dial goes with the day.
lines.master: The map dials belong to the plan; the clock dial belongs to the day.

lines.rookie: The night before the first of April is the last night of March.
lines.junior: The last night of March is the night before the first of April.
lines.master: The night before the first of April falls on the final night of March.

lines.rookie: Click! The box is locked. Only friends know the days.
lines.junior: Click! The box is locked, and only friends know the days.
lines.master: Click! The box is locked; only friends know the days.

lines.rookie: Below, the villages are dark and quiet.
lines.junior: Down below, the villages are dark and silent.
lines.master: Far below, the villages lie dark and silent.

lines.rookie: Then a small flame rises on Maebong hill.
lines.junior: Then a little flame starts to rise on Maebong hill.
lines.master: Then a small flame climbs into the dark on Maebong hill.

lines.rookie: Far away, on other hills, you see more lights.
lines.junior: In the distance, more lights appear on other hills.
lines.master: In the distance, one hilltop after another answers with its own light.

lines.rookie: First the night of the sign, then the day of the march.
lines.junior: The night of the sign comes first, and then the day of the march.
lines.master: The night of the sign must come first, the day of the march after it.

lines.rookie: March has thirty-one days. The night before April 1 is the last night of March.
lines.junior: March has thirty-one days, so the night before April 1 is the last night of March.
lines.master: March has thirty-one days; the night before April 1 is therefore the final night of March.

lines.rookie: The march is on the first of April, not the second.
lines.junior: The march is on the first of April, not on the second.
lines.master: The march falls on the first of April, not the second.

lines.rookie: That is Mr. Pyo's day. Two messengers said the first of April.
lines.junior: That is the day Mr. Pyo gave. Two messengers said the first of April.
lines.master: That is Mr. Pyo's false day. Two messengers agreed on the first of April.

lines.rookie: These numbers fit, but not in this order. The night of the sign comes first.
lines.junior: These numbers are right, but in the wrong order. The night of the sign is first.
lines.master: The numbers are right but misplaced. The night of the sign comes first.

lines.rookie: That night, Gwan-sun lights the fire on Maebong hill.
lines.junior: That night, Gwan-sun lights the fire up on Maebong hill.
lines.master: That night, Gwan-sun sets the fire blazing on Maebong hill.

lines.rookie: On 1 April 1919, thousands of people gather at Aunae Market.
lines.junior: On 1 April 1919, thousands of people come together at Aunae Market.
lines.master: On 1 April 1919, thousands of people gather in Aunae Market.

lines.rookie: Gwan-sun helps lead them, with the village elders. They call for independence.
lines.junior: Gwan-sun helps lead them, together with the village elders, and they call for independence.
lines.master: Alongside the village elders, Gwan-sun helps lead them as they call for independence.

lines.rookie: On 1 March 1919, people all over Korea called for independence. This is the March First Movement.
lines.junior: On 1 March 1919, people all over Korea called for independence, and this became the March First Movement.
lines.master: On 1 March 1919, people across Korea called for independence, in what we now call the March First Movement.

lines.rookie: The stranger waits at the station, on Mr. Pyo's wrong day. He never reads the plan.
lines.junior: The stranger waits at the station on Mr. Pyo's wrong day, so he never reads the plan.
lines.master: The stranger keeps watch at the station on Mr. Pyo's false day, and never reads the plan.

lines.rookie: No name, only a small flame. And the plan stayed safe.
lines.junior: No name, only a small flame, and the plan stayed safe.
lines.master: No name, only a small flame; and the plan stayed safe.

lines.rookie: Sunja
lines.junior: Sunja
lines.master: Sunja

lines.rookie: Gwan-sun
lines.junior: Gwan-sun
lines.master: Gwan-sun

lines.rookie: Okhui
lines.junior: Okhui
lines.master: Okhui

lines.rookie: Sunja writes only in Hangeul too. But her mark is a flower, not a flame.
lines.junior: Sunja writes only in Hangeul too, but her mark is a flower, not a flame.
lines.master: Sunja also writes only in Hangeul, yet her mark is a flower rather than a flame.

lines.rookie: Gwan-sun asked you to find the writer. Her notebook is not on the table.
lines.junior: Gwan-sun asked you to find the writer, and her notebook is not on the table.
lines.master: Gwan-sun is the one who asked you to find the writer; her notebook is not even on the table.

lines.rookie: Okhui writes in Chinese characters, and her mark is stars.
lines.junior: Okhui writes in Chinese characters, and she marks her name with stars.
lines.master: Okhui writes in Chinese characters, and stars, not a flame, mark her name.
